thread:
monitor-bot: ALERT — Unusual peering behaviour detected: CDN provider announced a leaking BGP route, large fraction of eu-west1 traffic being steered to SFO POP. Edge latencies up 3x, 5xxs on websocket sessions. Cost alert: egress jump. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/edge/route-leak-1768009999

sre-oncall: seeing the same. Websocket p95 ~2.4s, token refresh 502s. KMS latencies also ticked for some customer keys (maybe coincident).

infra-lead: tagging @network-eng. Do we have a confirmed BGP leak from CDN or from our cloud provider?

network-eng: CDN announced an emergency routing update in their status page, they flagged a bad announce to several IXs. It's external, TTL still high so cached routes persist for ~10m. Looks like SFO POP is saturated.

eng-runtime: impact: requests routed through that POP hit our ord1 cluster which is at 95% GPU allocator. We're hitting queueing + eviction. Canary and burst queues are failing over.

eng-ml: can we shift inference traffic away from ord1 quickly? We have warm pools in ord2 and iad1 but not fully provisioned.

infra-lead: plan A: CDN control-plane purge + reduce edge TTLs (if provider allows) to force rebalancing. Plan B: origin-side routing — advertise a higher weight on eu nodes so CDN will prefer them when routes update. Also start cross-region traffic-shift to iad1.

prod-ops: customers reporting errors in EU. Should we send an incident banner?

support-ops: yes - post now: "We're investigating increased errors and latency for EU customers; working on failover. No data loss expected." Keep it high level.

network-eng: sending purge request to CDN now. They say TTL change takes 30-120s to propagate but purges should help. Also opening a ticket with the CDN NOC for immediate reroute.

infra-lead: eng-runtime, start the ord1 -> iad1 traffic-shift. Use the weighted routing policy: set ord1 weight=20, iad1=80. Keep canary rate 1%. Exec: 
```
# run in infractl
infractl route set-weight --service inference --region ord1 --weight 20
infractl route set-weight --service inference --region iad1 --weight 80
```

eng-runtime: executing. Autoscaler note: increasing iad1 pool min to avoid CPU throttles. Running: 
```
infractl pool resize --region iad1 --min 24 --gpu-type a100
```

sre-oncall: also enabling temporary request-throttling on public endpoints to protect backend: 95th percentile token rate cap. Will also bump retry-backoff on SDK from 300ms -> 800ms via feature flag to reduce thundering herd.

eng-ml: for keys hitting KMS slow, fallback plan: if KMS latency >2s for a key we serve cached wrapped-key from local KMS cache for 10m; will revert when KMS healthy. Need approval for holding wrapped keys in RAM.

infra-lead: approve temporary wrapped-key cache for 10m TTL for affected customers only. Log and audit all uses. eng-runtime implement quick patch behind feature flag.

eng-runtime: patch deployed to prod-ff. Wrapped-key cache enabled for key-ids: [prod-eu-1, prod-eu-2]. Monitoring set.

network-eng: CDN purge acknowledged. They pushed a mitigation to withdraw the leaked announce from some IXs. Early signs: traffic rebalanced ~12% in last 2m.

eng-runtime: ord1 queue depth dropping, GPU eviction events reduced. P95 latency coming down to ~1.1s.

sre-oncall: cost note: cross-region egress will increase bill. Finance heads alerted. This is cheaper than prolonged 503s for customers.

prod-ops: banner update: "Mitigation in progress — traffic rerouted to alternate regions and we have temporary throttles in place. Expect intermittent errors to decline over next 30 minutes."

support-ops: fielding tickets. Suggested response snippet: "We're failing over traffic to other regions due to a third-party routing incident. If you see increased latency, please retry after 30s. No action required on your side."

network-eng: CDN confirms full withdraw of bad announce. They recommend lowering edge TTL back to normal after 15m of stability.

eng-ml: monitoring KMS latencies: trending down to baseline. Wrapped-key cache had ~120 hits, no auth anomalies.

infra-lead: rolling back temporary route weights to standard in 20m if stable. Also file postmortem with CDN ticket id and propose adding automated origin-side weight shifts for similar events.

sre-oncall: moving to #war-room for follow-ups. Good job team. :thumbsup:

monitor-bot: RESOLVED — CDN route leak mitigated by provider; edge traffic normalized. Incident duration ~28m. Postmortem link: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1768009999-bgp-route-leak
